findings.reason: Peer-trusted-transport variant, verified from source in snapshots/s01. UNTRUSTED SOURCE: hdlc_rx_greybus_frame() (drivers/greybus/gb-beagleplay.c:204-214) parses a Greybus message delivered by the remote peer MCU over the serdev UART/HDLC link (ADDRESS_GREYBUS dispatch in hdlc_rx_frame(), line 449); the attacker is the remote endpoint of this virtual-bus protocol, exactly the seed's threat model. MISSING LOCAL LIMIT CHECK: the peer-controlled 16-bit header field is extracted at line 208 (gb_msg_len = le16_to_cpu(gb_frame->hdr.size)) and passed as the delivered length to greybus_data_rcvd() at line 213, while the locally known real frame length — len = bg->rx_buffer_len - 4 computed at line 439 and passed in as the 'len' parameter — is entirely ignored; gb_msg_len is never compared to len, to the frame buffer, or to any kernel-known maximum for this receive path. The downstream validation is vacuous: gb_connection_recv() (drivers/greybus/operation.c:1027-1066) re-reads msg_size = le16_to_cpu(header.size) from the very same peer-supplied bytes (line 1049) and only tests 'if (size < msg_size)' (line 1050) — for this caller size == msg_size by construction, so the check can never fire; the validation fetch is not independent of the used value. UNSAFE USE: for a request-direction message, gb_operation_create_incoming() (operation.c:626-655) computes request_size = size - sizeof(header) and, after gb_operation_message_alloc() bounds message_size <= hd->buffer_size_max (operation.c:367-372, a per-host constant registered by gb_hd_create at gb-beagleplay.c:939 and clamped to <= U16_MAX at hd.c:155-158), executes memcpy(operation->request->header, data, size) (operation.c:648) — reading up to buffer_size_max peer-declared bytes from &gb_frame->hdr inside the fixed-size rx_buffer[MAX_HDLC] array of the heap-allocated struct gb_beagleplay (gb-beagleplay.c:81-83), when only len (~ a few hundred at most) bytes are valid. The response direction memcpy(message->buffer, data, size) (operation.c:1012) is capped at the locally known message_size = sizeof(header)+payload_size, but that copy still reads size bytes from the same rx_buffer, so any peer reply whose hdr.size exceeds the real HDLC payload drives an OOB read there too (peer controls result/errno, so the EMSGSIZE clamp to header-only is bypassable by setting result=0). CONSEQUENCE: remotely (peer-MCU) triggerable heap out-of-bounds read past the fixed rx_buffer array inside struct gb_beagleplay; the over-read bytes are copied into a gb_message and parsed by greybus protocol request handlers in workqueue context — kernel heap info disclosure into parsing state, with no OOB write identified because every destination buffer is allocated from the same peer size and bounded by buffer_size_max. Asymmetric-validation signal present: the TX/request-generation side of the same greybus core enforces GB_OPERATION_MESSAGE_SIZE_MAX (U16_MAX, include/linux/greybus/operation.h:45) and buffer_size_max at allocation time, but the beagleplay RX path never cross-checks the peer length against the bytes actually received. Counterevidence checked: es2.c USB-bridge sibling host driver is safe (cport_in_callback at es2.c:830-841 checks actual_length >= sizeof(*header) and actual_length is host-controller-truncated to transfer_buffer_length = ES2_GBUF_MSG_SIZE_MAX; arpc_in_callback at es2.c:1042 copies only fixed sizeof(*resp) after the same minimum check; apb_get_cport_count at es2.c:1221-1225 clamps the device-supplied cport count to U8_MAX), which shows the core API is safe when the caller passes a locally bounded length — the beagleplay caller is the component that supplies the unchecked peer length.

candidates.reason: Peer-field source: gb_msg_len = le16_to_cpu(gb_frame->hdr.size) taken from the remote MCU's HDLC-framed Greybus message; part of the reported finding.

Locally known limit that is ignored: hdlc_rx_frame() computes len = bg->rx_buffer_len - 4 (real received frame payload length, CRC-checked at 431-435) and passes it to hdlc_rx_greybus_frame(bg, buf, len) at line 449, but hdlc_rx_greybus_frame never uses len — the missing cross-check of the reported finding.

Vacuous validation: gb_connection_recv() re-reads msg_size from the same peer bytes it was handed as size, so 'if (size < msg_size)' at line 1050 cannot fire for the beagleplay caller; validated value is not independent of used value; part of the reported finding.

Consuming copy: memcpy(operation->request->header, data, size) in gb_operation_create_incoming() copies peer-declared size bytes from the fixed rx_buffer[MAX_HDLC] (gb-beagleplay.c:83) into the freshly allocated request message — destination bounded by buffer_size_max, source over-read; part of the reported finding.

cport_in_callback (es2.c:802-848) passes urb->transfer_buffer/urb->actual_length to greybus_data_rcvd; actual_length is set by the host controller and cannot exceed transfer_buffer_length (buffers allocated kmalloc(ES2_GBUF_MSG_SIZE_MAX) at es2.c:1342), and the >= sizeof(*header) minimum is enforced at es2.c:830, so the delivered length is locally bounded — no peer length beyond the controller-truncated value. This sibling host driver demonstrates the core API is safe with a bounded caller, isolating the defect to gb-beagleplay.c.

arpc_in_callback checks urb->actual_length >= sizeof(*resp) (line 1042) and then copies only the fixed struct size, memcpy(rpc->resp, resp, sizeof(*resp)), into a kzalloc'd struct from the ARPC_IN_SIZE_MAX-sized urb buffer (es2.c:1368); no peer-supplied variable length reaches a copy or allocation.

apb_get_cport_count() reads the device-supplied le16 cport count via usb_control_msg and clamps it before use: 'if (retval > U8_MAX) { retval = U8_MAX; ... }' (es2.c:1221-1225); num_cports drives ida_alloc_range with the clamped value — peer count properly cross-checked against a kernel-known limit.

hdlc_rx() byte-collection loop guards every store with 'if (bg->rx_buffer_len < MAX_RX_HDLC)' before writing rx_buffer[rx_buffer_len] (gb-beagleplay.c:481-484) and cc1352_bootloader_rx guards 'if (count > sizeof(bg->rx_buffer) - bg->rx_buffer_len)' (gb-beagleplay.c:620-633), so serdev RX accumulation into the fixed buffer is range-checked; the unchecked propagation happens only at line 208/213 via gb_msg_len.

limitations: Sweep bounded to the greybus transport family in s01: es2.c (USB-bridge host driver), gb-beagleplay.c (serdev/HDLC host driver), and the shared receive core operation.c/connection.c/hd.c were deep-read; other peer-transport reply handlers present in s01 (virtio/vhost vring processing, 9p trans_virtio/trans_fd/trans_xen/trans_rdma, nbd, ceph, cifs, rpmsg/qcom_glink, ntb, hv, mctp, virtio_rpmsg) were enumerated by directory listing only and not deep-read before the finalize directive.

Impact is bounded to a heap OOB read: destination buffers are allocated from the same peer-supplied size and enforced <= hd->buffer_size_max by gb_operation_message_alloc (operation.c:367-372), so no OOB write was identified on this chain; the over-read length is capped by buffer_size_max (beagleplay registers TX_CIRC_BUF_SIZE via gb_hd_create at gb-beagleplay.c:939, clamped <= U16_MAX at hd.c:155-158).
No runtime reproducer or compilation was performed (read-only snapshot; the transport requires a serdev UART peer MCU); the chain was verified by direct source reading of the cited lines only.

The exact numeric values of MAX_RX_HDLC/RX_HDLC_PAYLOAD and TX_CIRC_BUF_SIZE were not re-read before the finalize directive; the OOB-read bound is therefore expressed in terms of those constants (fixed compile-time array rx_buffer[MAX_HDLC] at gb-beagleplay.c:83) rather than concrete byte counts.

Whether the over-read bytes are exfiltrated back to userspace (e.g., via greybus protocol responses or debugfs) was not traced to the individual protocol request handlers; confidence is medium for the invariant violation and the OOB read, lower for end-to-end information disclosure.
